question: Should experimental Claws be permitted to register arbitrary stdio MCP commands and implicitly reuse exact global MCP declarations, or must both operations go through a host-authorized broker/allowlist and explicit sharing grant?
rationale: The branch creates privileged host configuration and executable-process declarations; choosing the permitted command set and cross-Claw sharing policy changes OpenClaw's security contract and cannot be resolved safely from implementation mechanics alone.

options.title: Require brokered, explicitly shared MCP resources
options.body: Permit only host-authorized or brokered stdio commands and require an explicit host grant before a Claw can adopt or share a global declaration.

options.title: Allow direct manifest MCP ownership
options.body: Accept manifest-provided commands and exact global reuse as an intentional experimental capability, with the resulting host-execution and tenancy risk owned by maintainers.

options.title: Defer MCP ownership from the Claws lifecycle
options.body: Land no MCP mutation support until the RFC or a narrower design establishes the authorization and isolation contract.

recommendation.title: Require brokered, explicitly shared MCP resources
recommendation.body: Permit only host-authorized or brokered stdio commands and require an explicit host grant before a Claw can adopt or share a global declaration.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR and have already established the lifecycle invariants that the authorization model must preserve.
